site.name: LivePlay
site.summary: LivePlay is free, open-source sound cue software for theatre, radio, live events and parties. It plays music and effects from a running order and instant carts, mixes them on a built-in mixer, and can trigger lights, mixers and video from the timeline. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.

features: Playlist of sound cues with groups, tabs and automatic running order
Cart player with up to 64 instant carts per page
Waveform trimming, fades, loops and volume automation
Automatic ducking under announcements and effects
Touch-friendly Show Mode that locks editing
Built-in mixer with buses, sends, EQ, gate, compressor and limiter
Show control events over OSC, MIDI, MIDI Show Control and HTTP
Behringer X Air mixer control and SMPTE timecode output
Local or remote operation across a network
User accounts, roles, API tokens and a REST and WebSocket API

faq.a: LivePlay is free, open-source sound cue software for theatre, radio, live events and parties. You line up music and effects in a playlist, fire each one at the right moment, and balance them on a built-in mixer.
Yes. LivePlay is free to download and use, with no licence fees, subscriptions or paid tiers. It is open source under the GNU AGPL-3.0 licence.

faq.q: Which operating systems does LivePlay run on?
faq.a: LivePlay runs on 64-bit Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13.3 or later on Apple Silicon and Intel, and 64-bit Linux as an AppImage, .deb or .rpm package.

faq.q: Which audio formats can LivePlay play?
faq.a: LivePlay plays WAV, AIFF, FLAC and MP3 audio files.

faq.q: Can LivePlay control lights, mixers and other show equipment?
faq.a: Yes. A cue can fire events from its timeline over OSC, MIDI, MIDI Show Control and HTTP, control Behringer X Air mixers and send SMPTE timecode. Tools such as Bitfocus Companion can also control LivePlay through its API.

faq.q: Can I run LivePlay across a network?
faq.a: Yes. The audio engine can run on one computer while other computers control it over the network. The sound comes from the engine, so the show keeps playing if a control computer drops out.

faq.q: Does LivePlay work with a touchscreen, keyboard or MIDI controller?
faq.a: Yes. Show Mode gives you large, touch-friendly controls and locks editing, and you can also run the show from your keyboard or a MIDI controller.
